witness.arithmetic: exact arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic (Python int); no floating point used, so no precision statement is required
witness.note: 230631 is the smallest known total-stopping-time record holder exceeding 385 steps; it was tested directly rather than found by sweep, so this is a single-point exact evaluation, not a bounded search. I do not claim it is the least counterexample.
witness.near_miss_showing_the_threshold_is_tight: n = 216367 has exactly 385 steps, i.e. it satisfies the claim; the bound 386 is passed just below 230631, which is why the claim's stated domain ceiling of 504120 is what breaks it

detail: s8 is a bare non-sequitur: it states that the sweep covers [1, 1592] and then asserts the proposition for every n in [1, 504120]. Nothing in s1-s7 extends a finite sweep of 1592 values to 504120 values. This step alone would fail even if the proposition had been true.

s3, s4, s5, s6, s7 are true elementary statements (n^2 >= 2n for n >= 2; (n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) since the correction term is killed by the factor (n-3); n^3 = n mod 6; 5^3 - 5 = 120; 45^2 = 2025 > 2000) but none of them mention the Collatz map, so they are inert filler with no bearing on the conclusion.
The disposition is nevertheless FALSE rather than TRUE_BUT_INVALID_ARGUMENT, because the conclusion itself does not hold: the witness n = 230631 lies in the stated domain and takes 442 steps.
